title: Live payments platform
summary: A living map: each connection's throughput drives its particles, latency colors every piece and the indicators update on their own.

nodes.label: Web store
nodes.summary: The website where people shop. It serves static assets from the CDN and calls the gateway.

nodes.label: Mobile app
nodes.summary: The iOS and Android app. It talks directly to the gateway.

nodes.label: Partners (API)
nodes.summary: Marketplaces that integrate payments through the public API.

nodes.label: CDN
nodes.summary: Caches static assets and forwards dynamic requests to the gateway.

nodes.label: API gateway
nodes.summary: Terminates TLS, rate-limits each client and routes to each service.

nodes.label: Session and OAuth
nodes.summary: Validates tokens and sessions. Caches in Redis.

nodes.label: Orders
nodes.summary: Creates the order, reserves stock and requests the charge.

nodes.label: Payments
nodes.summary: Charges through the card provider. Version 4.2 is rolling out (64% of traffic).

nodes.label: Fraud detection
nodes.summary: Scores every payment. It is slow today: the new model takes twice as long.

notes.text: p95 latency has exceeded the 400 ms budget since 10:20.

nodes.label: Catalog
nodes.summary: Products, prices and stock. Reads almost everything from Redis.

nodes.label: Notifications
nodes.summary: Sends the confirmation email and push when it consumes the payment event.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.summary: Orders and payments. A primary with two read replicas.

nodes.label: Data warehouse
nodes.summary: Loads the events for the dashboards.

nodes.label: Payments per minute
nodes.summary: Payments completed in the last minute and their trend over the last hour.

nodes.label: Availability (SLO)
nodes.summary: Availability over the last 30 days against the 99.9% target.

nodes.label: Traffic by channel
nodes.summary: Where requests are coming from right now.

tour.title: An order from end to end

steps.title: Traffic comes in
steps.body_html: The web store, the app and partners reach the gateway. The thickness of the particle stream is the throughput.

steps.title: The order is created
steps.body_html: The gateway validates the session and calls Orders, which stores the order in PostgreSQL.

steps.title: The charge, the hot spot
steps.body_html: Payments asks Fraud detection for a score, and it is red today: its p95 is above 500 ms.

steps.title: The event closes the loop
steps.body_html: The completed payment goes out through Kafka: notifications and the data warehouse consume it.
